findings.title: Argon2i missing minimum nb_blocks validation causes heap out-of-bounds write
findings.evidence: argon2i_32 (line 322) takes the caller-controlled nb_blocks, stores it into config.nb_blocks (line 328) with nb_lanes hard-coded to 1 (line 330), sizes the work area as malloc(nb_blocks * 1024) (line 345), and passes both to crypto_argon2 (line 347). Monocypher's contract requires nb_blocks >= 8 * nb_lanes (monocypher.h:160), but the wrapper never checks it. Inside crypto_argon2, segment_size = nb_blocks / nb_lanes / 4 and lane_size = segment_size * 4 (monocypher.c:749-750), so any nb_blocks in 0..3 yields lane_size == 0. The unconditional initialization loop 'FOR_T(u32, i, 0, 2) ... load64_le_buf(blocks[l * lane_size + i].a, hash_area, 128)' (monocypher.c:777-782) still writes two full 1024-byte blocks. Calling argon2i_32(1, 1, password, salt) therefore allocates only 1024 bytes at line 345 and writes 2048 bytes at monocypher.c:781, a 1 KB heap buffer overflow; nb_blocks == 0 makes it worse (malloc(0) then 2 KB of writes or a NULL dereference). Additionally 'blk *last_block = blocks + lane_size - 1' (monocypher.c:888) followed by store64_le_buf reads blocks[-1] for nb_blocks < 4, an out-of-bounds heap read. No precondition beyond calling this public API: any Python caller can supply a small nb_blocks, and the unsafe memory access happens inside the C call itself.

findings.title: Unchecked malloc result passed to crypto_argon2
findings.evidence: The work-area allocation at line 345 is never NULL-checked. nb_blocks is a caller-controlled uint32 field, so nb_blocks = 0xffffffff requests ~4 TiB from malloc (line 345), which can return NULL on memory-constrained systems. The NULL pointer is then handed to crypto_argon2 at line 347, where monocypher.c:751 does 'blk *blocks = (blk*)work_area;' and the initialization loop at monocypher.c:779-782 immediately dereferences and writes blocks[0]/blocks[1], producing a NULL-pointer dereference and process abort (denial of service). The argument is reachable directly from Python with no additional privileges or preconditions.
